newsitem.title: USA: GM CEO sees 1998 U.S. auto sales steady.
newsitem.headline: GM CEO sees 1998 U.S. auto sales steady.

text.p: General Motors Corp. Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Jack Smith said favorable economic conditions should allow U.S. vehicle sales in 1998 to remain at about 15 million units.

Smith, speaking to reporters following a dedication for a GM facility here, said high consumer confidence, low inflation and low unemployment are all contributing to the relatively strong vehicle sales.
"It's a good market," Smith said. "We look out now and we don't see anything on next year that would say we won't have another 15 million-car year."
Smith said the weakness of the yen against the dollar has made the pricing environment tougher for all automakers this year, which is holding prices down.
He added that GM is pleased with the sales performance of new models it has recently introduced, which he said will help GM in its fight for improved market share.

Smith talked to reporters after the dedication of GM's Service Parts Operations new world headquarters here. The division is responsible for marketing of GM and AC-Delco replacement parts and accessories.
